**Surat al-Ikhlas** (the Chapter of Sincerity) is Meccan [[Ibn al-Duraysi and Ibn Jarir reported from Abu al-'Aliyah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: They said, "Describe your Lord to us for us," so Jibril brought this surah: (Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge). And al-Tabarani and Abu al-Shaykh in al-'Azamah reported from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Quraysh said, "O Messenger of Allah, describe your Lord to us," and Allah revealed (Say: He is Allah, the One). See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/669-670, and the narrations that follow.]] In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾ Abu al-'Aliyah narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b that the polytheists said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), "Describe your Lord to us," so Allah the Exalted revealed this surah [[Reported by al-Tirmidhi in the Tafsir, the Tafsir of Surat al-Ikhlas: 9/299-300, and also reported as a mursal narration: 9/301; and by Imam Ahmad: 5/134; al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/540, and al-Dhahabi agreed; and al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa al-Sifat: 1/419; and al-Tabari: 30/342.]].

Abu Zabyan and Abu Salih narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl and Arbad ibn Rabi'ah came to the Prophet (ﷺ). 'Amir said, "To what do you invite us, O Muhammad?" He said, "To Allah." He said, "Describe Him to us. Is He of gold? Or of silver? Or of iron? Or of wood?" So this surah was revealed, and Allah destroyed Arbad with a thunderbolt and 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl with plague. We have mentioned this in Surat al-Ra'd [[See what preceded: 4/301.]].

Al-Dahhak, Qatadah and Muqatil said: Some of the rabbis of the Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "Describe your Lord to us, O Muhammad, so that perhaps we may believe in you, for Allah revealed His description in the Torah. Tell us: of what substance is He? Does He eat and drink? And from whom does He inherit?" So Allah revealed this surah [[Reported by al-Tabari: 30/342-343. See also al-Fath al-Samawi: 3/1135; al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/671.]].

﴿Say: He is Allah, the One.﴾ That is, "Wahid" (One). There is no difference between "wahid" and "ahad" (both meaning one). This is indicated by the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "Say: He is Allah, the Wahid" [[Abu Hayyan said in al-Bahr al-Muhit: 8/528: "Ahad with the meaning of wahid."]].

﴿Allah, the Samad.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "al-Samad" is the One who has no hollow (no inside), i.e., who has no internal cavity.

al-Sha'bi said: He is the One who does not eat and does not drink.

It was also said: its explanation is what follows it. Abu al-'Aliyah narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: "al-Samad" is the One who has not begotten and has not been begotten, because whoever is begotten will die, and whoever inherits is inherited from Him [[Reported by al-Tabari: 30/346.]].

Abu Wa'il Shaqiq ibn Salamah said: He is the Master whose mastery has reached its completion. This is also the narration of 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He is the Master who has been perfected in all kinds of mastery [[Reported by 'Abd al-Razzaq in the Tafsir: 2/407, and al-Tabari: 30/346.]]. And from Sa'id ibn Jubayr also: He is the Perfect in all His attributes and actions. It was also said: He is the Master to whom one turns in needs. And al-Suddi said: He is the One sought in desires, the One invoked for help in calamities. The Arabs say: "Samadtu fulanan asmuduhu samadan" (with the sukun on the mim), meaning "I intended him," and the one intended is "samad" (with a fatha on the mim) [[The bracketed text is missing from "B".]].

Qatadah said: "al-Samad" is the One who remains after the annihilation of His creation. 'Ikrimah said: "al-Samad" is the One above whom there is no one, and this is the view of 'Ali. al-Rabi' said: He is the One to whom calamities do not attach. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: He is the One in whom there is no defect.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 112, verses 3–4:

﴿He neither begets nor is He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him, anyone.﴾ Ḥamzah and Ismāʿīl read "kufuwan" (كُفُؤًا) with a silent fāʾ and a hamza. Ḥafṣ, on the authority of ʿĀṣim, read it with a ḍammah on the fāʾ and without a hamza. The others read it with a ḍammah on the fāʾ and with a hamza. All of these are valid dialectal forms (lughāt ṣaḥīḥah), and its meaning is "the equal" (al-mithl), i.e., He is One.

It is also said: this is an inversion of word order (al-taqdīm wa-al-ta'khīr). Its underlying sense is: "and there was not anyone equal to Him" (wa-lam yakun lahu aḥadun kufuwan), meaning a likeness (mithlan).

Muqatil said: The polytheists of the Arabs said, "The angels are the daughters of Allah." The Jews said, "ʿUzayr is the son of Allah." The Christians said, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." So Allah refuted them, and He negated from His essence both begetting and a likeness.

Al-Malīḥī informed us, from Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Nuʿaymī, from Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Abū al-Yamān, from Shuʿayb, from al-Zuhrī, from Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, the Exalted, said: The son of Adam denies Me, though it is not for him to do so, and reviles Me, though it is not for him to do so. As for his denying Me, it is his saying, 'He will not restore me as He originated me,' and the first creation is no easier for Me than its restoration. As for his reviling Me, it is his saying, 'Allah has taken a son,' whereas I am the One, the Eternal Refuge (al-Ṣamad), who has not begotten nor been begotten, and there is none comparable to Me, anyone."

Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad al-Sarakhsī informed us (folio 205/b), from Abū ʿAlī Ẓāhir ibn Aḥmad, from Abū Isḥāq al-Hāshimī, from Abū Muṣʿab, from Mālik, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Ṣaʿṣaʿah al-Anṣārī, from his father, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī: that a man heard another man reciting "Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad" and repeating it. When morning came, he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him, as if the man regarded it as little. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "By Him in whose hand my soul is, it is indeed equal to a third of the Qur'an."

Abū Saʿīd al-Shurayḥī informed us, from Abū Isḥāq al-Thaʿlabī, from Abū Bakr Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Iṣfahānī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaʿfar ibn Aḥmad ibn Fāris, from Yūnus ibn Ḥabīb, from Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī, from Shuʿbah, from Qatādah: I heard Sālim ibn Abī al-Jaʿd narrate from Maʿdān ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from Abū al-Dardāʾ, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Is one of you unable to recite a third of the Qur'an in a night?" I said, "O Messenger of Allah, who can manage that?" He said, "Recite: Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad."

Al-Sarakhsī informed us, from Ẓāhir ibn Aḥmad, from Abū Isḥāq al-Hāshimī, from Abū Muṣʿab, from Mālik, from ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿUbayd ibn Jubayr, client of Zayd ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, that he said: I heard Abū Hurayrah say: I came along with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he heard a man reciting, "Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad, Allāhu al-Ṣamad, lam yalid wa-lam yūlad, wa-lam yakun lahu kufuwan aḥad." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "It is certain (wajabat)." I asked, "What, O Messenger of Allah?" He said, "Paradise." Abū Hurayrah said: I wanted to go to the man to give him the good news, but I feared that I would miss the midday meal with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so I preferred the meal. Then I went to the man and found that he had gone.

Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṣāliḥī informed us, from Abū Bakr Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ḥīrī, from Ḥājib ibn Aḥmad al-Ṭūsī, from ʿAbd al-Raḥīm ibn Munīb, from Yazīd ibn Hārūn, from al-Mubārak ibn Faḍālah, from Thābit, from Anas, who said: A man said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "I love this surah: Qul huwa Allāhu aḥad." He said: "Your love for it has caused you to enter Paradise."
